texts.preamble: Mohit Kumar vs District Magistrate Haridwar & Others on 27 November, 2019 Author: Alok Kumar Verma Bench: Ramesh Ranganathan, Alok Kumar Verma In The High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital Writ Petition (M/S) No. 3221 of 2019 Mohit Kumar .......Petitioner Versus District Magistrate Haridwar & others .......Respondents Mr. Anil Kumar Dabral, Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. J.C. Pande, Brief Holder for the State. Mr. Ashutosh Thakral, Advocate for the respondent no.2. Judgment
texts.facts: This Writ Petition is filed questioning the oral direction allegedly issued by the District Magistrate, Haridwar prohibiting the sale of chicken within the territorial limits of Haridwar district. 2. The petitioner, who is running a chicken centre in Laksar, claims that such direction of the District Magistrate, Haridwar is unauthorized and is contrary to law. 3. In the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of the Food Safety Officer, Laksar, Haridwar district, it is stated that the petitioner does not have a valid registration certificate regarding the Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006; as per Rule 2.5.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, 'chicken' also falls within its ambit; the District Magistrate, Haridwar had only sought to implement the orders passed by the High Court from time to time and, therefore, no interference is called for. The State Government was also directed to ensure that no Slaughter House was permitted to run without complying with the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011.
texts.arguments: 5. While Mr. Anil K. Dabral, learned counsel for the petitioner, would contend that the petitioner Mohit Kumar vs District Magistrate Haridwar & Others on 27 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12283476/ 1 has a valid registration certificate, the order of the Division Bench in Writ Petition (PIL) No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018 prohibits operation of illegal Slaughter Houses and the slaughter of animals. The action being taken by the District Magistrate, Haridwar, to prohibit sale of chicken does appear to be in compliance with the order of the Division Bench in Writ Petition (PIL) No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018. 6. Mr. Anil K. Dabral, learned counsel for the petitioner, would contend, placing reliance on the supplementary affidavit filed by him, that sale of meat and chicken continues unabated in the other districts of the State.

Mr. Anil K. Dabral, learned counsel for the petitioner, would contend, placing reliance on the supplementary affidavit filed by him, that sale of meat and chicken continues unabated in the other districts of the State.
